subject.title: Decouple mode="session" from thread binding requirement

question: Should OpenClaw support persistent native/ACP child sessions without channel thread binding, and what contract should own parent delivery, follow-up routing, cleanup, and visibility?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the desired behavior changes the meaning of persistent sessions across native subagents, ACP, channel delivery, and high-power task ownership; automation should not choose those semantics alone.

options.title: Design unbound persistent sessions
options.body: Keep this issue open and implement a core contract for unbound persistent sessions before relaxing the guards in native and ACP spawn paths.

options.title: Keep thread-bound session only
options.body: Leave `mode="session"` tied to thread/current-conversation binding and improve docs/error copy around `mode="run"`, `sessions_send`, and ACP resume workarounds.

options.title: Scope ACP separately
options.body: Track only ACP non-thread affinity in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/55484 and keep native subagent session semantics unchanged for now.

recommendation.title: Design unbound persistent sessions
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and implement a core contract for unbound persistent sessions before relaxing the guards in native and ACP spawn paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session-thread management and source/doc updates make this the best available owner for deciding the cross-path contract.
